messages.content: G'day mate! What can I do for ya today?
why does your speed in response very so much?

Ah, good question! The response speed can vary 'cause of a few reasons:

- How complex your question is — more complicated stuff takes a bit longer to think through.
- Server load — sometimes the AI servers get busy, so it slows down a bit.
- Network lag — if your internet's a bit crook or the servers are far away, that adds delay.
- Also, sometimes I’m just being a cheeky slowpoke, but mostly it’s the above.

If you want me to speed up on simpler stuff, just shout!

## ⏱️ Pipeline Timing
| Stage | Duration | Timestamp |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Prompt Build | 1ms | 00:14:56.943 |
| LLM API Call | 3.03s | 00:14:56.944 → 00:14:59.971 |
| Post-Process | 0ms | |
| **Total Round-Trip** | **3.03s** | |

Yeah, that 3-second LLM API call is the main culprit. The AI's busy chewing through your prompt, hitting the servers, then spitting out the answer. Sometimes it’s quick, sometimes it’s slow depending on server load and complexity.

If it’s consistently slow, might be worth checking your connection or the server status. But 3 seconds ain’t too shabby for a brainy AI doing its thing!
maybe if i passed the chat payload first with an option to retireve the rest of the page it would be faster as im sure the llm remembers context of conversation even if its one api call at a time?

Spot on, mate! Sending the chat payload upfront with an option to fetch more context later could speed things up. The LLM does keep some context memory per call, so if you give it enough to work with initially, less back-and-forth needed.

It’s like prepping your tools before starting the job — less faffing around. Plus, chunking the conversation lets you grab just what you need when you want, keeping calls lean and quick.

Smart thinking! If you want, I can help sketch out how to do that.
this is so interesting lets ask chatgbt go there now
lets ask chat gbt how it behaves when used as an api if it remembers the system prompt for example the inittial this is who you are through api calls or it really forgets everything

Righto, here’s the gist from ChatGPT about using it as an API:

- It does *not* remember the system prompt or chat history across separate API calls automatically.
- Each API call is stateless — it treats every request as brand new.
- To keep context, you gotta include the full message history (system prompt, user messages, assistant replies) every time you call it.
- The system prompt only applies for that single request; if you want it remembered, resend it with each API call.
- No hidden memory or backend persistence between calls.
- The Conversations API variant can keep persistent conversation state with an ID, but regular Chat Completions API doesn’t.

So yeah, you’re spot on — you gotta manage the context yourself and feed it in each call to keep the convo going.

Want me to fetch the official docs link or a code snippet for how to do this?
na so if we pass through the persona and the chat and we give it an option to retrieve the page for context we could cause half the time we talking about whats in the page

Exactly, mate! If you pass the persona (system prompt) and chat history with each call, and only fetch the full page context when needed, you save a stack of time and tokens.

Half the convo is just about what’s on the page, right? So why keep shoveling all that every time? Just grab the page context when you actually need to dive deep.

Smart way to keep it snappy and efficient. Bloody clever!
ok write out a whole prompt i can ask my mate about to make a plan for a spec for the app to implement this

No worries, here’s a prompt you can chuck to your mate to get the ball rolling on a spec for the app idea:

---

Hey [Mate’s Name],

I’ve been thinking about how we can speed up our ChatGPT API calls and keep the convo smooth. Here’s the rough plan:

- We send the system persona (the “this is who you are” prompt) plus recent chat history with each API call to keep context fresh.
- Instead of loading the whole page content every time, we add an option to fetch the full page context only when needed.
- This way, most calls are quick and lean, and we only get heavy when the convo actually needs deep page info.
- We should figure out how to chunk and cache the page context smartly so the app knows when to fetch more.
- Let’s also plan for managing token limits by trimming old chat history or summarising it.

Can you help sketch out a spec for this workflow? We want something clear to build from.

Cheers!

---
